title: The Tragedy of the Red Woman
notes: Episode 755's subtitle file is missing locally (only 0754.txt and 0756.txt were available); the murder discovery closes 0754 and 0756 opens with a recap narration plus the attack-on-Kawana aftermath already having happened offscreen between the two available files, so the exact blow-by-blow of that attack is reconstructed from 0756's dialogue/flashbacks rather than seen directly. Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Ran, Sonoko, Masumi Sera) omitted by convention -- note that one key behavioral clue (Kawana handing the newly-arrived Masumi Sera the villa photos without asking which of the group she was, proving Kawana already knew/suspected Sera was the detective) is preserved in clue c5's description even though Sera herself has no node. The old lower-fidelity case file (cases/ep754-756_the_tragedy_of_the_red_woman.json) got the culprit right (Sumika Kawana) but flattened the case drastically: it omitted the entire fifteen-year-old original murder (an unnamed wife killing her unnamed husband in a jealous rage, becoming 'the Red Woman'), omitted Shinobu Kagawa (the murdered man's mistress, who has spent fifteen years hunting the Red Woman and is who actually attacked Kawana, mistaking her red-clothed disguise for the real thing), omitted the reporting-error clue chain (Inspectors Yamato and Morofushi, and retired officer Uehara) that identifies Kagawa, and mischaracterized event e1: it wasn't Hakuya arranging a prank alone -- Satoko Imoto and Hakuya jointly planned the Red-Woman prank, Imoto died fleeing in a panic after Kagawa mistook her red costume for the real Red Woman and gave chase, and Hakuya's cowardly silence about the prank for twelve years is Kawana's actual motive. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: The tomatoes weren't missing from the tub, just sunk: plain sugar-heavy tomatoes sink, but the same tomatoes float once the water's salinity is raised with bath salts -- proving the tub was clear when checked and secretly filled afterward.
Twelve-year-old photo shows Satoko Imoto in a beige cardigan, but she was found wearing a long red coat -- she had been dressed as the Red Woman herself, not attacked by one.

The old police report says the Red Woman stabbed the officer and escaped, but the officer's actual memory is she threw the knife and fled -- meaning someone else must have retrieved the knife and later planted it by the swamp.
Kawana's sleeves were down when the group first met but rolled up after the murder, and dried salt crystals cling to them from stirring bath salts into the tub.

Everyone else mistook the newly arrived detective for a boy, but Kawana handed her the villa photos without asking anything -- proof she already knew, from eavesdropping earlier, that the visitor was a girl detective.
